cases.reviewerAnswer: Saber expresses factual knowledge; conocer expresses familiarity: Sé dónde vive Ana; conozco a Ana; conozco Madrid.
cases.notes: An appropriate introductory contrast, rather than an exhaustive account of both verbs.

cases.reviewerAnswer: Sé is the stressed first-person present form of saber; pronominal se is unstressed and has no written accent.
cases.element: content.body.scope.noteUk: "Вимова однакова, значення розрізняє лише графічний наголос."
cases.defect: The explanation erases the stress distinction: verbal sé is tonic, while pronominal se is atonic. They share their segmental sounds, but their pronunciation in connected speech is not identical in stress.
cases.correction: Explain that the sounds are the same but stress differs: "Sé — наголошена форма дієслова saber, а займенник se — ненаголошений. На письмі їх розрізняємо знаком наголосу: sé / se."
sources: RAE/ASALE, Ortografía de la lengua española (2010), chapter II, treatment of tilde diacrítica in monosyllables, including sé/se and tonic versus atonic words (from memory).
cases.notes: The examples and written forms themselves are correct.

cases.reviewerAnswer: Conozco a Ana; veo a mis padres; veo al profesor. Ordinary inanimate direct objects do not take personal a.
cases.notes: The scope appropriately mentions the usual tener/hay exceptions.

cases.reviewerAnswer: coger → cojo; recoger → recojo; escoger → escojo. The spelling change preserves the consonant sound.
conocer → conozco; conducir → conduzco; traducir → traduzco
cases.notes: The wording "Більшість" correctly avoids claiming that every vowel + -cer/-cir verb follows this pattern.

cases.reviewerAnswer: coger: take; catch or take transport. First-person present: cojo.
cases.notes: The regional qualification is appropriately limited to part of Latin America.

cases.reviewerAnswer: conducir: drive a vehicle; yo conduzco.
conocer: know or be acquainted with; meet or get to know. First-person present: conozco.
decir: say or tell; yo digo, tú dices.
poner: put or place; put on television or music. First-person present: pongo.
recoger: collect or pick up; tidy up. First-person present: recojo.
saber: know information; saber + infinitive: know how to. First-person present: sé.
venir: come; yo vengo, tú vienes.
Expected content: present forms in -go, -zco and -jo; the venir, decir, saber, dar and ver paradigms; sé/se; saber/conocer; personal a.

cases.element: task.hints[1].blocks[0].text: "Завтра я сідаю на потяг о дев’ятій."
cases.defect: El tren de las nueve identifies the nine-o'clock train by its scheduled departure. The translation instead attaches nine o'clock to the speaker's boarding action, losing the distinction between de las nueve and a las nueve.
cases.correction: Preserve the train's departure time: "Завтра я їду потягом, що відправляється о дев’ятій."
sources: Packet task.prompt[1].text: "Mañana ___ (coger, yo) el tren de las nueve."
Review duties: check wrong meaning and translations.
RAE/ASALE, Nueva gramática de la lengua española (2009), treatment of prepositional noun modifiers and temporal adjuncts (from memory).
cases.notes: The conjugation key, error feedback and Spanish reveal are correct.

cases.reviewerAnswer: Expected forms include pongo, salgo, traigo, hago; conozco, conduzco, traduzco; cojo, recojo, escojo; vengo, digo, sé, doy and veo, with their corresponding present paradigms.
cases.notes: The opening statement about other persons being regular applies to the verb set in the immediately following table.
